text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT - Elevated restart rate on inference pods in pool gpu-pool-west-2. Symptoms: GPU OOM during prefill on long-context requests, followed by container exits (code 137) and occasional node kernel GPU faults. Paging nina_oncall.

nina_oncall: on it. seeing increased 5xxs on /v1/chat for model=gpt-xl-long. Which node(s)?

sam_sre: affected nodes: n-prod-gpu-11, n-prod-gpu-12. Pattern: large single prefill (user transcript ingestion ~80k-200k tokens) causes KV cache allocations to spike then CUDA allocation fails. Also observed Xid GPU errors intermittently.

lee_runtime: paste snippet from pod log + dmesg:
```
[2026-03-15T20:10:02Z] inference: prefill: reserving 12.1GB for kv_cache
[2026-03-15T20:10:02Z] inference: cudaMalloc returned CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T20:10:03Z] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 79
kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:00:1:0: GPU fault detected: reason 79
containerd: container exited with code 137
```

tanya_infra: Xid 79 indicates a GPU page fault, often heap+OOM. I'm concerned about node kernel reporting combined with restarts -> possible driver/kernel interaction under sustained mem pressure.

jordan_cs: We have two customers reporting failures: MediStream (large audio transcripts) and LegalEase (court record ingestion). They've seen a mix of timeouts and hard failures. CS is elevating to SEs.

mona_product: MediStream is on a batch ingestion workflow that sometimes packs full-day transcripts into one request. We need a stop-gap while we investigate.

nina_oncall: immediate mitigations we can attempt now:
- apply request-level prefill admission control (reject > 100k tokens with friendly 413 + guidance)
- enable runtime prefill_kv_eviction for large requests (evict older KV pages during prefill)
- move heavy traffic to a fallback quantized variant with lower memory footprint
- taint the two nodes to prevent new pods being scheduled while we drain them
- add temporary autoscale to spin up extra safe nodes (gpu-pool-west-3)
Which should we do in what order?

sam_sre: My priority: taint + drain nodes to stop further kernel faults, enable prefill admission, and route heavy customers to fallback. I can taint n-prod-gpu-11/12 now.

tanya_infra: I'll prepare an autoscale push to gpu-pool-west-3 and ensure AMI has updated driver 525.116 which fixed a similar bug last quarter. Recommend we don't reboot all nodes immediately; do staged roll for driver.

lee_runtime: runtime toggles:
```
# runtime flags
prefill_admission.enabled=true
prefill_admission.max_tokens=100000
prefill_kv_eviction.enabled=true
fallback_model=gpt-xl-q4
```
I'll flip admission control and kv_eviction on 15% of traffic first, then 100% if stable.

nina_oncall: go for it. sam, taint/drain cmds?

sam_sre: running:
```
kubectl taint nodes n-prod-gpu-11 node-oom=true:NoSchedule
kubectl cordon n-prod-gpu-12
kubectl drain n-prod-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Draining n-prod-gpu-12 now.

sam_sre: (reacted :white_check_mark:) n-prod-gpu-12 drained. n-prod-gpu-11 tainted. Scheduling no new pods.

deploy-bot: No active infra deploys.

lee_runtime: admission and kv_eviction enabled on canary fleet. Early telemetry: canary pods show 30% reduction in peak GPU memory for long requests; no OOMs in 8m window.

jordan_cs: Notifying MediStream + LegalEase with temporary workarounds: split uploads or use chunked ingestion. Email sent.

mona_product: Also flagging SDK change: add client-side guard to chunk > 50k tokens by default. We'll ship a patch to the JS SDK as low-risk fix.

nina_oncall: scaling: tanya, can we add 6 instances to gpu-pool-west-3 quickly? We need capacity to absorb drained pods.

tanya_infra: launching 6 nodes now (type p4d-small), estimated ready 6m. Driver image includes 525.116.

lee_runtime: After successful canary, promoting runtime flags to 100% for gpt-xl-long. Also enabling automatic fallback to gpt-xl-q4 when prefill estimation > threshold.

nina_oncall: good. monitoring for regressions. sam, capture node-level coredumps and gpu-smi logs and upload to s3.

sam_sre: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/1769009998/gpu-logs.tar.gz. Added pointers in the incident tracker.

jordan_cs: customers acknowledged temporary mitigation; MediStream requested ETA for SDK timeline.

mona_product: I'll draft a customer-facing summary once we have root-cause.

lee_runtime: follow-ups for engineering:
- add per-request KV memory estimator to runtime (pre-check alloc and reject early)
- implement incremental prefill (stream blocks of tokens and commit KV gradually)
- add Xid-tracing to map GPU faults to request IDs
- expand long-context perf tests to 200k token simulations in staging

nina_oncall: handoff summary for next shift: cause = oversized prefill (80k-200k) causing KV cache allocations to exceed GPU memory, triggering CUDA OOM and occasional Xid GPU faults leading to container restarts and node instability. Actions taken: tainted/drained nodes, enabled prefill admission control (max_tokens=100000), turned on kv_eviction and fallback model routing, scaled up temporary pool, notified customers, collected logs, created post-incident ticket INF-1769009998-prefill-oom.

sam_sre: current metrics: prefill-related OOM errors down from 2.8% -> 0.2%. Pod restarts on affected nodes stopped after drains.

tanya_infra: next 24h plan: roll driver update to remaining gpu-pool-west nodes in canary, enable node-level GPU memory pressure alerts, and add kernel param tweaks recommended by vendor.

lee_runtime: we'll prioritize the KV estimator and progressive prefill in the 2-week sprint.

jordan_cs: will follow up with customers tomorrow with detailed remediation steps and recommended SDK usage.

mona_product: creating product ticket for SDK changes and longer-term UX for long-sessions.

nina_oncall: closing active pager; status -> MONITORING. If OOM > 0.5% over 10m, re-pager will fire. Keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status -> MONITORING. Postmortem assigned to sam_sre and lee_runtime.

(sam_sre reacted :spiral_note_pad:)
